entries.name: attachPolicyLogger
entries.signature: export declare function attachPolicyLogger(policy: Policy<unknown, unknown>, logger: PolicyLogger, policyName?: string): () => void;
entries.jsdocSummary: Attach structured logging to a resilience policy. Subscribes to retry, circuit breaker, timeout, success, and failure events when available.

entries.name: backgroundJobPolicy
entries.signature: export declare const backgroundJobPolicy: ResiliencePolicy;
entries.jsdocSummary: Resilience policy tuned for background job processing where higher latency and more retries are acceptable.

entries.name: backoff
entries.signature: export declare const backoff: { /** * Waits `base`, then twice as long before each later retry: `base * 2^(attempt - 1)`, * capped at `max`, varied by `jitter`. * * @example backoff.exponential({ base: 200, max: 5000, jitter: 0.25 }).upTo(3) */ exponential(options: ExponentialBackoffOptions): Backoff; /** * Waits the same `ms` before every retry. * * @example backoff.constant(60_000).upTo(1) */ constant(ms: number): Backoff; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Builders of a {@link Backoff}. Every builder retries forever until `upTo` limits it.

entries.name: Backoff
entries.signature: export type Backoff = { /** * The wait in milliseconds before retry number `attempt` (1 for the first retry) after * `reason` failed the previous try: the error it threw, or the failure it returned. * `undefined` means stop: do not retry. Throws `InvalidBackoffError` when `attempt` is * not a whole number from 1. */ delay(attempt: number, reason: unknown): number | undefined; /** The most retries this backoff allows: what `upTo` set, or `Infinity`. */ readonly maxRetries: number; /** The same backoff, stopping after at most `retries` retries. `upTo(0)` never retries. */ upTo(retries: number): Backoff; /** * The same backoff, also retrying returned failures of these `@arki/failure` * definitions. Thrown errors keep retrying as without `while`; other returned * failures are not retried. Short for * `while(reason => !isFailure(reason) || definitions.some(d => d.is(reason)))`. * * @example backoff.exponential({ base: 100 }).while(DbTimeout, ExportUnavailable) */ while(...definitions: RetryableFailures): Backoff; /** * The same backoff, retrying only the reasons for which `predicate` returns true. A * reason is a thrown error or a returned failure, so the predicate sees both: a * returned failure is retried only when a predicate says yes to it. A negative * predicate such as `reason => !(reason instanceof BadInput)` says yes to failures too. * * @example backoff.exponential({ base: 100 }).while(reason => reason instanceof NetworkError) */ while(predicate: RetryPredicate): Backoff; };
entries.jsdocSummary: How long to wait before each retry, and when to stop. Immutable: `upTo` and `while` return a new backoff. Each call narrows the backoff, except that the first `while` decides alone whether a returned failure is retried.

entries.name: BreakEvent
entries.signature: export type BreakEvent = FailureReason | { isolated: true; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Fired when a circuit breaker opens. `isolated` means it was opened by hand.

entries.name: BulkheadPolicy
entries.signature: export type BulkheadPolicy = Policy & { /** Fires when a call is turned away because both the slots and the queue are full. */ readonly onReject: PolicyEvent<void>; };

entries.name: BulkheadPolicyOptions
entries.signature: export type BulkheadPolicyOptions = { /** Maximum concurrent executions (default: 10) */ maxConcurrent?: number; /** Maximum queue size for pending executions (default: 100) */ maxQueue?: number; };

entries.name: BulkheadRejectedError
entries.signature: export declare class BulkheadRejectedError extends ResilienceError { readonly code: "ARKI_RESILIENCE_E004"; readonly remediation = "Retry later, raise the bulkhead limits, or shed load before the call."; constructor(message?: string, options?: ErrorOptions); }
entries.jsdocSummary: A bulkhead turned the call away: every execution slot and queue slot was taken.

entries.name: CancelledError
entries.signature: export declare class CancelledError extends ResilienceError { readonly code: "ARKI_RESILIENCE_E003"; readonly remediation = "Check signal.aborted before you start, or catch CancelledError where you abort."; constructor(message?: string, options?: ErrorOptions); }
entries.jsdocSummary: The caller's own signal aborted while the call was in flight. `cause` is the signal's reason.

entries.name: CircuitBreakerPolicy
entries.signature: export type CircuitBreakerPolicy = Policy & { readonly onBreak: PolicyEvent<BreakEvent>; /** Fires when the breaker lets a trial call through after `halfOpenAfter`. */ readonly onHalfOpen: PolicyEvent<void>; /** Fires when a trial call succeeds and the breaker closes again. */ readonly onReset: PolicyEvent<void>; };

entries.name: CircuitBreakerPolicyOptions
entries.signature: export type CircuitBreakerPolicyOptions = { /** Duration in milliseconds before the breaker transitions from open to half-open (default: 30_000) */ halfOpenAfter?: number; /** Number of consecutive failures before the breaker opens (default: 5) */ consecutiveFailures?: number; };

entries.name: CircuitOpenError
entries.signature: export declare class CircuitOpenError extends ResilienceError { readonly code: "ARKI_RESILIENCE_E001"; readonly remediation = "Wait for the breaker to half-open and try again, or serve a fallback while it is open."; constructor(message?: string, options?: ErrorOptions); }
entries.jsdocSummary: The circuit breaker is open: the call was rejected without running the function.

entries.name: createBulkheadPolicy
entries.signature: export declare function createBulkheadPolicy(options?: BulkheadPolicyOptions): BulkheadPolicy;
entries.jsdocSummary: Create a bulkhead (concurrency-limiter) policy.

entries.name: createCircuitBreakerPolicy
entries.signature: export declare function createCircuitBreakerPolicy(options?: CircuitBreakerPolicyOptions): CircuitBreakerPolicy;
entries.jsdocSummary: Create a circuit breaker policy using consecutive-failure detection.

entries.name: createResiliencePolicy
entries.signature: export declare function createResiliencePolicy<Mapped = never>(options?: ResiliencePolicyOptions<Mapped>): ResiliencePolicy<Mapped>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Create a composed resilience policy: [bulkhead ->] retry -> circuit breaker -> timeout.

entries.name: createRetryPolicy
entries.signature: export declare function createRetryPolicy<Mapped = never>(options?: RetryPolicyOptions<Mapped>): RetryPolicy<Mapped>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Create a retry policy. It calls the function, and after each failure asks `backoff` how long to wait before the next try, or whether to stop and rethrow the error.

entries.name: createTimeoutPolicy
entries.signature: export declare function createTimeoutPolicy(options?: TimeoutPolicyOptions): TimeoutPolicy;
entries.jsdocSummary: Create a timeout policy that aggressively cancels the operation when the deadline is exceeded.

entries.name: databasePolicy
entries.signature: export declare const databasePolicy: import("./policy.js").Policy<never, import("@arki/clock").SleepFailure>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Resilience policy tuned for database operations.

entries.name: definePresets
entries.signature: export declare function definePresets<N extends string>(options: Record<N, ResiliencePolicyOptions>): Presets<N>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Build one composed policy per name. Each name has its own breaker, so one failing downstream does not open the circuit of another. A `Presets` object shared by two apps shares its breakers too: same downstream, same health.

entries.name: ExponentialBackoffOptions
entries.signature: export type ExponentialBackoffOptions = { /** The wait before the first retry, in milliseconds. Each later wait doubles. */ readonly base: number; /** The longest wait, in milliseconds. Default and upper bound: `MAX_TIMER_MS` (about 24.8 days). */ readonly max?: number; /** * How much each wait may vary, from 0 (the default: exact) to 1. With `0.25` a wait is * picked at random from 75% to 125% of its exact value, then capped at `max`. Spreads * the retries of many clients so they do not hit a recovering service at once. */ readonly jitter?: number; /** * Where jitter gets its randomness: a function returning a number in [0, 1), like the * default `Math.random`. Pass a fixed one to make jittered waits deterministic in tests. */ readonly random?: () => number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Options of {@link backoff.exponential}.

entries.name: externalApiPolicy
entries.signature: export declare const externalApiPolicy: ResiliencePolicy;
entries.jsdocSummary: Resilience policy tuned for external API calls (geocoding, AI providers, etc.).

entries.name: FailureEvent
entries.signature: export type FailureEvent = { /** Wall-clock time of the call in milliseconds. */ duration: number; /** Whether the policy handled this failure (retried it, counted it, …). */ handled: boolean; reason: FailureReason; };

entries.name: FailureReason
entries.signature: export type FailureReason = { error: unknown; } | { value: unknown; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Why a call counted as a failure: the error it threw, or the value it returned (a failure from `@arki/failure`).

entries.name: InvalidBackoffError
entries.signature: export declare class InvalidBackoffError extends ResilienceError { readonly code: "ARKI_RESILIENCE_E006"; readonly remediation = "Pass finite, non-negative numbers: jitter from 0 to 1, a whole number to upTo, attempts from 1."; constructor(message: string); }
entries.jsdocSummary: A `backoff` builder got an option or an attempt number it cannot use. Raised where the backoff is built.

entries.name: isBrokenCircuitError
entries.signature: export declare function isBrokenCircuitError(error: unknown): error is CircuitOpenError;

entries.name: isBulkheadRejectedError
entries.signature: export declare function isBulkheadRejectedError(error: unknown): error is BulkheadRejectedError;

entries.name: isResilienceError
entries.signature: export declare function isResilienceError(error: unknown): error is ResilienceError;
entries.jsdocSummary: True for every error raised by the resilience layer itself.

entries.name: noop
entries.signature: export declare const noop: Policy;
entries.jsdocSummary: A policy that only runs the function. Useful as a default or in tests.

entries.name: OnThrow
entries.signature: export type OnThrow<Mapped> = (error: unknown) => Mapped | PromiseLike<Mapped>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Turns a thrown error that reaches the caller into a value, usually a failure from `@arki/failure`. Rethrow the errors it does not recognise, so they stay bugs.

entries.name: Policy
entries.signature: export type Policy<F = never, E = never> = PolicyExecution<F, E> & { /** Fires once per call that ends well, even when that took retries. */ readonly onSuccess: PolicyEvent<SuccessEvent>; /** Fires on every failed attempt the policy sees. */ readonly onFailure: PolicyEvent<FailureEvent>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Execution plus observable policy events.

entries.name: PolicyCallback
entries.signature: export type PolicyCallback<T> = (context: PolicyContext) => PromiseLike<T> | T;
entries.jsdocSummary: The function a policy runs.

entries.name: PolicyContext
entries.signature: export type PolicyContext = { /** * Aborted when the caller's signal aborts or when a timeout policy reaches its * deadline. A timeout policy also aborts it once the function has returned. */ readonly signal: AbortSignal; /** 0 for the first call and 1 for the first retry. Always 0 when the policy has no retry. */ readonly attempt: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What a wrapped function receives on every call.

entries.name: PolicyEvent
entries.signature: export type PolicyEvent<E> = (listener: (event: E) => void) => Subscription;
entries.jsdocSummary: An event method: pass a listener, get a subscription back.

entries.name: PolicyExecution
entries.signature: export type PolicyExecution<F = never, E = never> = { /** Phantom: makes a policy with a fallback unassignable to a plain `Policy`, so `wrap` rejects it. */ readonly [fallbackType]?: () => F; readonly [outcomeType]?: () => E; execute<T>(this: void, fn: PolicyCallback<T>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T | F | E>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Any policy: runs a function and reports how each call ended. `F` is what a fallback may resolve instead of the function's own `T`; it is `never` for a plain policy.

entries.name: PolicyLogger
entries.signature: export type PolicyLogger = { info(message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>): void; warn(message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>): void; error(message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>): void; };

entries.name: Presets
entries.signature: export type Presets<N extends string = string> = Readonly<Record<N, ResiliencePolicy>>;
entries.jsdocSummary: A registry of named composed policies. `N` is the union of the names.

entries.name: RESILIENCE_ERROR_CODES
entries.signature: export declare const RESILIENCE_ERROR_CODES: { /** * The circuit breaker is open and rejected the call. * * @fix Wait for the breaker to half-open and call again, or serve a fallback with `withFallback` while it is open. * @verify cd packages/resilience && bun run test */ readonly circuitOpen: 'ARKI_RESILIENCE_E001'; /** * A timeout policy reached its deadline. * * @fix Raise `timeoutMs`, or make the operation faster. Pass the policy's `signal` to the work so it stops. * @verify cd packages/resilience && bun run test */ readonly timeout: 'ARKI_RESILIENCE_E002'; /** * The caller's own signal aborted the call. * * @fix Check `signal.aborted` before you start, or catch `CancelledError` where you abort. It is not an outage. * @verify cd packages/resilience && bun run test */ readonly cancelled: 'ARKI_RESILIENCE_E003'; /** * A bulkhead had no free execution or queue slot. * * @fix Retry later, raise `maxConcurrent` or the queue size, or shed load before the call. * @verify cd packages/resilience && bun run test */ readonly bulkheadRejected: 'ARKI_RESILIENCE_E004'; /** * Every retry attempt failed. * * @fix Read `lastError` for the real cause, or raise the `upTo` limit. * @verify cd packages/resilience && bun run test */ readonly retriesExhausted: 'ARKI_RESILIENCE_E005'; /** * A `backoff` builder got an option or an attempt number it cannot use. * * @fix Pass finite, non-negative numbers: `jitter` from 0 to 1, a whole number to `upTo`, attempts from 1. * @verify cd packages/resilience && bun run test */ readonly invalidBackoff: 'ARKI_RESILIENCE_E006'; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Stable error codes of `@arki/resilience`. Match on the code, never on the message.

entries.name: ResilienceComponents
entries.signature: export type ResilienceComponents = { readonly retry: RetryPolicy; readonly circuitBreaker: CircuitBreakerPolicy; readonly timeout: TimeoutPolicy; /** Set only when the `bulkhead` option was given. */ readonly bulkhead?: BulkheadPolicy; };
entries.jsdocSummary: The parts a composed resilience policy runs. Their events fire on every composed call.

entries.name: ResilienceError
entries.signature: export declare abstract class ResilienceError extends Error { /** Stable machine-readable code, `ARKI_RESILIENCE_E<nnn>`. */ abstract readonly code: ResilienceErrorCode; /** What to do about it, in one sentence. */ abstract readonly remediation: string; constructor(message: string, options?: ErrorOptions); }
entries.jsdocSummary: Base class of every error the policies raise themselves. Errors thrown by your function pass through untouched.

entries.name: ResilienceErrorCode
entries.signature: export type ResilienceErrorCode = (typeof RESILIENCE_ERROR_CODES)[keyof typeof RESILIENCE_ERROR_CODES];
entries.jsdocSummary: The code of a {@link ResilienceError}.

entries.name: ResiliencePolicy
entries.signature: export type ResiliencePolicy<F = never> = Policy<F, SleepFailure> & { readonly components: ResilienceComponents; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What `createResiliencePolicy` returns: the composed policy plus the parts it runs. `F` is what its `onThrow` may answer instead of the function's own `T`; `never` without one.

entries.name: ResiliencePolicyOptions
entries.signature: export type ResiliencePolicyOptions<Mapped = never> = { /** When to retry and how long to wait first. Default: the `createRetryPolicy` default. */ retry?: Backoff; /** Whose timer the retry delay waits on. Default: the system clock. */ clock?: Clock; circuitBreaker?: CircuitBreakerPolicyOptions; timeout?: TimeoutPolicyOptions; /** * Limit concurrent calls. Off unless given, so existing callers keep unlimited * concurrency. It wraps everything else: one logical call, retries included, * holds one slot. */ bulkhead?: BulkheadPolicyOptions; /** * Map a thrown error that reaches the caller to a value, usually a failure from `@arki/failure`. * The call then resolves to `T | Mapped` instead of throwing. It wraps everything, so it also * sees an open circuit (`CircuitOpenError`), a deadline (`TimeoutError`) and a full bulkhead * (`BulkheadRejectedError`). A cancel by the caller's signal is never mapped. Rethrow the * errors it does not recognise, so they stay bugs. */ onThrow?: OnThrow<Mapped>; };

entries.name: RetriesExhaustedError
entries.signature: export declare class RetriesExhaustedError extends ResilienceError { readonly code: "ARKI_RESILIENCE_E005"; readonly remediation = "Read lastError for the real cause, or raise the attempt limit."; readonly attempts: number; readonly lastError: Error | undefined; constructor(attempts: number, lastError?: Error); }
entries.jsdocSummary: Thrown when all retry attempts have been exhausted without a successful result.

entries.name: RETRY_WAIT_FAILURES
entries.signature: export declare const SLEEP_FAILURES: readonly [import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"clock.sleep_cancelled", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"failure.unexpected_defect", undefined>];
entries.jsdocSummary: Exact canonical failure definitions returned by Clock.sleep.

entries.name: RetryEvent
entries.signature: export type RetryEvent = FailureReason & { /** The retry about to run: 1 for the first retry. */ attempt: number; /** Backoff delay in milliseconds before that retry. */ delay: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Fired before each retry, after the failed attempt and before the backoff delay.

entries.name: RetryPolicy
entries.signature: export type RetryPolicy<F = never> = Policy<F, SleepFailure> & { readonly onRetry: PolicyEvent<RetryEvent>; /** * Fires when the last attempt has failed and its error, or its failure after at least one * retry, is about to reach the caller. A returned failure that was never retried does not fire it. */ readonly onGiveUp: PolicyEvent<FailureReason>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A retry policy. `F` is what its `onThrow` may answer instead of the function's own `T`; `never` without one.

entries.name: RetryPolicyOptions
entries.signature: export type RetryPolicyOptions<Mapped = never> = { /** * When to retry and how long to wait first. Default: * `backoff.exponential({ base: 100, max: 10_000, jitter: 0.25 }).upTo(3)`. */ backoff?: Backoff; /** Whose timer the retry delay waits on. Default: the system clock. Pass a `MockClock` to make tests instant. */ clock?: Clock; /** * Map an error that outlasts the retries, or one that is not retried, to a value. The call then * resolves to `T | Mapped` instead of throwing. A cancel by the caller's signal is never mapped. */ onThrow?: OnThrow<Mapped>; };

entries.name: RetryWaitFailure
entries.signature: export type SleepFailure = ReturnType<(typeof SLEEP_FAILURES)[number]>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Every operational outcome of Clock.sleep, inferred from its definitions.

entries.name: Subscription
entries.signature: export type Subscription = { dispose(): void; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Returned by every event method. Call `dispose()` to stop listening.

entries.name: SuccessEvent
entries.signature: export type SuccessEvent = { /** Wall-clock time of the call in milliseconds. */ duration: number; };

entries.name: TimeoutError
entries.signature: export declare class TimeoutError extends ResilienceError { readonly code: "ARKI_RESILIENCE_E002"; readonly remediation = "Raise the timeout, or make the operation faster."; constructor(message?: string, options?: ErrorOptions); }
entries.jsdocSummary: A timeout policy reached its deadline before the function returned.

entries.name: TimeoutPolicy
entries.signature: export type TimeoutPolicy = Policy & { readonly onTimeout: PolicyEvent<void>; };

entries.name: TimeoutPolicyOptions
entries.signature: export type TimeoutPolicyOptions = { /** Timeout duration in milliseconds (default: 30_000) */ timeoutMs?: number; };

entries.name: withFallback
entries.signature: export declare function withFallback<F, G = never, E = never>(policy: Policy<G, E>, fallback: (error: unknown) => F | PromiseLike<F>): Policy<G | F, E>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Give a policy a last answer. When the policy's call fails, `fallback` gets the error and its result becomes the result of the call. Put it outermost: inside `wrap` it would hide the errors the retry needs, so `wrap` does not accept a policy with a fallback.

entries.name: withResilience
entries.signature: export declare function withResilience<T, F = never, E = never>(fn: PolicyCallback<T>, policy: Policy<F, E>): Promise<T | F | E>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Execute a function with an already-constructed resilience policy.

entries.name: withRetry
entries.signature: export declare function withRetry<T, Mapped = never>(fn: PolicyCallback<T>, options?: RetryPolicyOptions<Mapped>): Promise<T | Mapped | SleepFailure>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Execute a function with a retry policy (no circuit breaker or timeout).

entries.name: withTimeout
entries.signature: export declare function withTimeout<T>(fn: PolicyCallback<T>, options?: TimeoutPolicyOptions): Promise<T>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Execute a function with a timeout policy.

entries.name: wrap
entries.signature: export declare function wrap<E = never>(first: Policy<never, E>, ...rest: Policy<never, E>[]): Policy<never, E>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Compose policies from the outside in: `wrap(retry, breaker, timeout)` retries a call whose every attempt goes through the breaker and then the timeout. Events on the result are those of the outermost policy.

entries.name: resilience
entries.signature: export declare function resilience<N extends string>(presets: Presets<N>): import("@arki/dot/plugin").AuthoredPlugin<import("@arki/dot/plugin").WireNeeds<import("@arki/dot/plugin").EmptyShape>, import("@arki/dot/plugin").ProvidedValues<{ resilience: ResilienceService<N>; }>, import("@arki/dot/plugin").EmptyShape, "resilience", { resilience: ResilienceService<N>; }, import("@arki/dot/plugin").EmptyPhases, import("@arki/dot/plugin").DotLoggingHandle<undefined>, undefined>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Build a DOT plugin that publishes the presets as `services.resilience` and logs their policy events at `debug` under `arki:resilience`.

entries.name: RESILIENCE_PLUGIN_ERROR_CODES
entries.signature: export declare const RESILIENCE_PLUGIN_ERROR_CODES: { /** * `for` or `run` got a name that is not in the presets (only reachable from untyped JS). * * @fix Use a name you passed to `definePresets(...)`. Types catch this in TypeScript. * @verify cd packages/resilience && bun run test */ readonly unknownPreset: 'ARKI_RESILIENCE_PLUGIN_E001'; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Stable error codes thrown by the resilience plugin. Match on these, never on the message.

entries.name: ResilienceService
entries.signature: export type ResilienceService<N extends string> = { /** The preset called `name`. The same object as `presets[name]`, so breaker state is shared. */ for(name: N): ResiliencePolicy; /** Run `fn` through the preset called `name`. */ run<T>(name: N, fn: PolicyCallback<T>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T | SleepFailure>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Services published by the resilience adapter.
